parts:
Hi,

I am trying to use aroma.affymetrix to analyze GWSNP 6.0, and I
followed the scripts in total copy number analysis 5.0 & 6.0:

library(aroma.affymetrix)

cdf<-AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType("GenomeWideSNP_6",tags="Full")
chipType<-"GenomeWideSNP_6"
name<-"SNPpractice"
cs<-AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name,chipType=chipType)
acc<-AllelicCrosstalkCalibration(cs)
csC<-process(acc)
plm<-AvgCnPlm(csC,mergeStrands=TRUE, combineAlleles=TRUE,shift=+300)

When I try to print print(plm), it shows
AvgCnPlm:
Data set: SNPpractice
Chip type: GenomeWideSNP_6,Full
Input tags: ACC,ra,-XY
Output tags: ACC,ra,-XY,AVG,+300,A+B
Parameters: (probeModel: chr "pm"; shift: num 300; flavor: chr
"median"; mergeStrands: logi TRUE; combineAlleles: logi TRUE).
Path: plmData/SNPpractice,ACC,ra,-XY,AVG,+300,A+B/GenomeWideSNP_6
RAM: 0.00MB


I am not sure about what "median" means in flavor: chr "median";

Thanks a lot,
Lixia

See ?AvgPlm, but it basically says that the mean chip effect estimates
is calculated using the median estimator. The alternative is to use
the sample mean (flavor="mean"), which is less robust.

I'm finalizing a version of the CRMA method for GWS5/GWS6, similar to
the one we published for 500K (and 10K & 100K) and writing up the
manuscript. It will of course take some months before it get
published, but that will explain all the details. This updated CRMA
method will involve other steps not mentioned in the vignette you are
referring - steps that improves things quite a bit actually.

Cheers

Henrik

> analysis(5.0 & 6.0)" section mentions that units on ChrX & ChrY are
> excluded from the model fit and all probes not on ChrX and ChrY all
> have the same average for all arrays(=2200), while it also mentions
> that all units are still calibrated. I don't understand this part. If
> the units on ChrX & ChrY are excluded from the model fit, how can they
> also be calibrated?

The details are explain in the CRMA paper:

H. Bengtsson; R. Irizarry; B. Carvalho; T. Speed, Estimation and
assessment of raw copy numbers at the single locus level,
Bioinformatics, 2008. [pmid: 18204055] [doi:
10.1093/bioinformatics/btn016]

but basically any normalization/calibration method can be though of as
having one step estimating the systematic effect, and one step that
corrects for that effect. Often we do not want to have ChrXY data to
affect the estimate of the systematic effects, so we estimate the
effects using all other data points instead. Then we assume that this
same effect is also affecting data on ChrXY, meaning we can apply the
same correction that was estimated to such data points as well.

Cheers,

/Henrik

parts:
Hi,

Thank you so much. I read the reference you mentioned and one question
come after it. For the allelic crosstalk model (equation 1), you try
to estimate the parameters (a_i, S_i) for each particular nucleotide
pair. Then get \hat{a_i} and \hat{S_i} and then get the estimate
\hat{x_ijk}. So my question is in GWSNP 6.0, it is rescaled all, does
that mean the model is not fitted to each particular nucleotide pair
but to all probes? The all probes not on ChrX and ChrY all have same
average for all arrays(=2200) means average the estimated average of
all probes equals to 2200 for all arrays? which is average of
\hat{x_ijk} for all j, k (include A, B and all nucleotide pair) equals
to 2200?

Thanks a lot,
Lixia

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: "median" meaning for AvgCnPlm model "parameter:(.... flavor: Chr "median") "
parts: Hi,

On Thu, Aug 14, 2008 at 1:20 PM, lixia <dia...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi,
>
> Thank you so much. I read the reference you mentioned and one question
> come after it. For the allelic crosstalk model (equation 1), you try
> to estimate the parameters (a_i, S_i) for each particular nucleotide
> pair. Then get \hat{a_i} and \hat{S_i} and then get the estimate
> \hat{x_ijk}. So my question is in GWSNP 6.0, it is rescaled all, does
> that mean the model is not fitted to each particular nucleotide pair
> but to all probes?
It is fitted to each pair separately. More below.

> The all probes not on ChrX and ChrY all have same
> average for all arrays(=2200) means average the estimated average of
> all probes equals to 2200 for all arrays? which is average of
> \hat{x_ijk} for all j, k (include A, B and all nucleotide pair) equals
> to 2200?

The crosstalk model is fitted for each of the six possible nucleotide
pairs separately (for the SNP units of course). Then, for each pair
the probe-pair signals are backtransformed based on the model fit such
that the estimated offset is subtracted and the crosstalk is removed.
This is the same for 10K, 100K, 500K, GWS5 and GWS6. For CN probes
(on GSW5 and GWS6) we subtract the average offset of the six pairs.
At this stage the calibration is only controlling for within-array
effects, but not between arrays.

To control from across array effects, we rescale *all* PMA and PMB
signals such that the average *on the autosomal chromosomes* becomes
2200 (it could have been any constant). For 10K-500K containing only
SNP units this was done pair by pair. For GWS5 and GWS6 we cannot do
this (too complicated to explain), but instead we rescale *all* PMs
such that the average *on the autosomal chromosomes* becomes 2200.
The average is estimated using the median estimator.

Cheers

/Henrik

On Fri, Aug 22, 2008 at 9:32 PM, lixia <dia...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi,

> algorithm of your CRMA paper. I have one question:
>
> To do the calibration, you try to fit the model (1) first, which is
> y*_ijk=a_i+S_ix_ijk + \epison_ijk. Here, a_i, S_i and x_ijk are all
> unknown. Although you mention later that either x_ijkA or x_ijkB is
> zero for homozygote(i,j) data points, I am still comfused about how to
> estimate a_i and S_i.

in words the model is estimated by finding the two homozygote arms
that "best" fit the data. What we mean by best is harder to explain.
The objective function allows for some data points outside the cone,
and pretty much ignores what is going on inside. The estimator is
robust. The method give more weight to data close to the "corner".
All this is done using an iterative re-weighted approach.

The model/algorithm was written Pratyaksha Wirapati back in 2001 for
calibrate four channel sequencing data but he later generalized it to
fit simplexes in any dimension. It is still on the to do list to
write this work up and publish it. Earlier this year, Pratyaksha
revisited this work again and have made more improvements and
modifications, and it is on the todo list to get this in a manuscript
and publish it. Without that document, it will be hard to be more
precise about the algorithm used.

Also, in the current implementation of aroma.affymetrix, we are
actually fitting a simplex (i.e. a triangle in 2D) and then we ignore
the "distant" edge/side (this is an suboptimal estimator, but we found
it a-good-enough working solution).

That's all I can offer for now

Henrik
